ext.custom_domains.admin.help.concepts.a: A Cloudflare token used to create and delete DNS records. One key can back many domains.
ext.custom_domains.admin.help.concepts.r: Leave nests and eggs unchecked to offer a domain to every game, or check specific ones to limit who can use it.
ext.custom_domains.admin.help.concepts.s: The SRV prefix (e.g. _minecraft._) that tells clients how to find the server. Auto-detected per game; override per egg if needed.
ext.custom_domains.admin.help.concepts.z: The domain as it exists in Cloudflare. The zone ID can be left blank — it is resolved automatically from the API key on first use.
ext.custom_domains.admin.help.intro: This module lets you offer branded, player-friendly domains. You curate a catalog of parent domains backed by Cloudflare; server owners then create subdomains on them, and the panel provisions the real DNS records for them.
ext.custom_domains.admin.help.step1.body: Under API Keys, store a Cloudflare API token with DNS edit permission for the zones you will use. Tokens are write-only and never shown again.
ext.custom_domains.admin.help.step2.body: Under Domains, add each parent domain, link it to its Cloudflare zone and API key, and optionally restrict it to specific games.
ext.custom_domains.admin.help.step3.body: Set the SRV service tag and per-egg overrides so Minecraft- and Rust-family servers get the correct records automatically.
ext.custom_domains.admin.help.step4.body: In Settings, turn the module on. Once enabled, the Custom Domains tab appears on servers whose game is allowed.

ext.custom_domains.server.help.intro: Custom domains let players connect using a friendly address like play.example.com instead of a raw IP and port.
ext.custom_domains.server.help.records.a: The right record type is chosen automatically based on your game — you only need to change it if you know you want something different.
ext.custom_domains.server.help.records.c: Points the domain at your server; players usually connect with the domain plus :port.
ext.custom_domains.server.help.records.s: Lets players connect with just the domain (no :port). Recommended for Minecraft-family servers.
ext.custom_domains.server.help.step1.bod: Choose one of the parent domains your host has made available, then type the subdomain label you want in front of it.
ext.custom_domains.server.help.step2.bod: When you add a mapping we automatically create the matching DNS records at the domain's provider and point them at your server.
ext.custom_domains.server.help.step3.bod: A mapping starts as Pending, becomes Active once the records are live, or Failed if something went wrong — the error is shown so you can fix it or retry with Re-sync.
ext.custom_domains.server.help.step4.bod: Once a mapping is Active, share the full domain with your players. Use the copy button next to each entry.
ext.custom_domains.server.help.title: Custom domains — quick guide
ext.custom_domains.server.subtitle: Point a friendly domain at this server so players don't need the IP and port.

ext.custom_domains.setting.proxied.help: Off is correct for game servers: proxying only supports HTTP and HTTPS traffic.
